cards.text: This prayer comes with a label on top: it's for one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his lament before the LORD. No name, no title, just a worn-out man talking straight to God. He opens with “Hear my prayer, O LORD; let my cry for help come before You.”

cards.question: The worn-out man asks the LORD to take His time and answer him whenever He's ready.

cards.text: He begs God not to hide His face from him in his day of distress, and to “answer me quickly when I call.” Friend, this man isn't leaving a voicemail, he's hitting redial again and again and AGAIN.

cards.question: Then the man tells God why he's in such a hurry. He says his days vanish like smoke. What's he saying about his life?

answers.text: Its troubles will blow over soon

cards.text: His bones burn like glowing embers. His heart is afflicted, withered like grass, and friend, I thought MY worn-down edges were rough.

cards.question: The man's heart is so worn down that he says he even forgets to ___ his bread.

cards.text: Through his loud groaning, his skin hangs on his bones. I live in a BAKERY with cookie dough on every spoon, so friend, I have NEVER forgotten to eat, not ONCE.

cards.question: The man calls himself a desert owl, an owl among the ruins, and a lone bird on a housetop. What do these pictures say about how he feels?

answers.text: He feels ready to fly home

cards.text: He says he lies awake, like a lone bird on a housetop. Friend, I did years of lying awake in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, the view is MOSTLY dust.

cards.question: Besides feeling all alone, the man has enemies, but they only bother him once in a while.

cards.text: All day long they taunt him, ridicule him and curse him. He says he has eaten ashes like bread and mixed his drink with tears, and friend, that is the saddest menu I have EVER heard.

cards.question: The man has been eating ashes like bread and mixing his drink with tears. What does he say all this sorrow comes from?
The man says it was his enemies who picked him up and cast him aside.

cards.text: No, he tells the LORD, “You have picked me up and cast me aside.” Friend, as a stamper who got carried across a kitchen and tucked into a junk drawer, I FELT that one.

cards.question: The man says his days are like lengthening shadows. Then he goes back to the picture he used for his heart and says he withers away like ___.

cards.text: Then the whole prayer turns on one little word: But. The man's days are like lengthening shadows, but the LORD is a whole different story.

cards.question: The man's own days are fading. What does he say about the LORD?

answers.text: He is far off and silent
He has grown tired of Zion

cards.text: His renown endures to all generations, too. Then the man turns to Zion, the city of Jerusalem, and tells the LORD He will rise up and have compassion on her.

cards.question: The man says Zion will have to wait a long time for the LORD's favor, because her appointed time hasn't come yet.

cards.text: Nope, “the appointed time has come.” God's servants delight in Zion's stones and take pity on her dust.

cards.question: When the LORD shows Zion favor, the man says the nations will fear the name of the LORD.
God's servants take pity on Zion's dust. Then the man says the LORD will ___ Zion.
Right after saying the LORD has appeared in His glory, the man says the LORD will despise the prayer of the destitute.

cards.text: No, He will turn toward their prayer, and “He will not despise their prayer.” Then the man wants all this written down for the generation to come.

cards.question: Why does the man want this written down for the generation to come?

answers.text: So people not yet created can praise the LORD
So everyone will remember his own name
So his enemies will finally go quiet

cards.text: I bet he never pictured a cookie stamper with a giant French mustache reading it, friend. Then he tells how the LORD looked down from the heights of His sanctuary, from heaven to earth.

cards.question: The LORD gazed out from heaven to earth. What did He look down to hear?
The LORD heard a prisoner's groaning. He also looked down to ___ those condemned to death.

cards.text: All so that they may proclaim the name of the LORD in Zion and praise Him in Jerusalem, when peoples and kingdoms assemble to serve the LORD. Friend, that's a LOT of people in one place, and not one of them is there for the cookies.
Whew, friend. The man comes right back down to his own trouble, and he doesn't hold back: “He has broken my strength on the way; He has cut short my days.”

cards.question: His strength is broken and his days are cut short. What does the man ask God?

answers.text: Not to take him in the middle of his days
To take him home right away
To send his enemies far away

cards.text: Then he talks about God's years, which go on through all generations. In the beginning God laid the foundations of the earth, and the heavens are the work of His hands, and friend, I get proud of ONE good batch.

cards.question: The earth and the heavens are the work of God's hands. The man says they will perish and all wear out like a ___.

cards.text: Then he tells God, “But You remain the same, and Your years will never end.” Friend, I wore out on a kitchen counter, and He outlasts the HEAVENS.

cards.question: The man ends his prayer by saying the children of God's servants will have to live in fear.

findings.problem: This card cites Psalm 102:11-12 and repeats 'The man's days are like lengthening shadows.' Stop 1 card 15 already told that line from verse 11, so it is recapped here. Verse 11 also falls outside stop 2's range of 102:12-28. The card should carry only the turn on 'But' into verse 12.

The question asks 'Why does the man want this written down for the generation to come?' The word 'this' points back to the previous story card, which the baker can no longer see. The question doesn't say what is being written down.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'So people not yet created can praise the LORD', is the only one that uses Bible wording ('not yet created', 'praise the LORD'), and it is the longest. The wrong answers are plain modern phrasing ('remember his own name', 'finally go quiet'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: God's years, the creation line, and the joke attached to it. It is not the opening card, so it is limited to 1 to 2 sentences. It also packs verses 24 and 25 into one card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
